subject: Life Skills
title: How Credit Cards Really Work
description: One-minute skill: How Credit Cards Really Work.

hook.text: She paid the minimum on a $3,000 balance. At 22% APR, it will take her 15 years and cost $4,700 in interest alone.

buildup.text: Credit cards offer a grace period: pay in full each month and interest is zero. Miss it, and the rate hits hard.

discovery.text: Minimum payments are designed to maximize interest profit. They keep you in debt as long as legally possible.

twist.text: Rewards points are funded by people carrying balances. If you pay in full, you profit from the system.

climax.text: Use credit cards only for what you can pay in full this month.

punchline.text: Pay in full or pay a fortune. There is no middle ground.

quiz.question: Why are minimum payments dangerous?
options: They damage your credit score immediately
They are designed to keep you in debt as long as possible, maximizing interest
They count as missed payments on your credit report
